overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The committee's withholding of June 12, 2018 executive session minutes under attorney-client privilege was no longer subject to the OML, and the AG declined to judge the privilege claim, which belongs to the Supervisor of Records.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee improperly withheld its June 12, 2018 executive session minutes in their entirety under attorney-client privilege.
allegations.key_passage: Because the executive session minutes are no longer being withheld under the Open Meeting Law, we find no violation of that law.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued that at least the litigation party names and nature of the claims were not privileged, so the privilege assertion was challenged.
allegations.key_passage: While the Open Meeting Law authorizes the Attorney General to investigate a complaint alleging a violation of the law, it does not give us the authority to determine whether the Committee's assertion of the attorney-client privilege was justified.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
